items.stem: What is meant by "Invoice (bill)"?
items.answer: Document prepared by the seller for a credit sale, giving the details of goods sold and the amount due from the buyer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Document prepared by the seller for a credit sale, giving the details of goods sold and the amount due from the buyer.

An invoice is issued for every cash sale.
A debit note is issued by the seller when he receives returned goods.
A receipt is given by the person paying the money.

items.stem: Gupta Brothers returns damaged mobile accessories worth ₹4,000 to its supplier Sharma Traders and informs it that its account has been debited. Which source document is used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Debit note. A debit note is sent to the supplier for purchase returns.

items.stem:
The accountant of Sharma Industries prepares vouchers for: (a) payment of ₹8,000 rent in cash; (b) cash of ₹12,000 received from a customer; (c) credit purchase of a machine from Joshi Industries; (d) salary paid partly in cash and partly by cheque.
(i) Identify the type of voucher for each. (ii) Why are vouchers needed at all?
items.answer: (i) (a) Debit (cash payment) voucher (b) Credit (cash receipt) voucher (c) Transfer voucher (d) Complex (compound) voucher. (ii) They are documentary evidence supporting each entry, needed for checking and audit.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) (a) Debit (cash payment) voucher (b) Credit (cash receipt) voucher (c) Transfer voucher (d) Complex (compound) voucher. (ii) They are documentary evidence supporting each entry, needed for checking and audit.

items.stem: State any three types of accounting vouchers.
items.answer: Cash voucher; Debit voucher; Credit voucher; Transfer voucher; Complex (compound) voucher
items.markingKey: Any three of: Cash voucher; Debit voucher; Credit voucher; Transfer voucher; Complex (compound) voucher (1 mark each).

items.stem:
Aisha, who runs Singh Traders, does not issue cash memos for cash sales because "customers never ask for them". At the year end the tax officer questions the sales figure.
(i) What problem does the lack of source documents create? (ii) Advise Aisha on two practices to follow.
items.answer: (i) Sales cannot be verified; the records lose objectivity and reliability, and are not acceptable evidence for tax. (ii) Issue a serially numbered cash memo for every cash sale; file all vouchers date-wise and record entries only from vouchers.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Sales cannot be verified; the records lose objectivity and reliability, and are not acceptable evidence for tax. (ii) Issue a serially numbered cash memo for every cash sale; file all vouchers date-wise and record entries only from vouchers.

items.stem: Show the accounting equation on the basis of the following transactions of Manish: (1) Commenced business with cash ₹2,50,000. (2) Purchased goods for cash ₹1,35,000. items.stem: Varun started business with cash ₹4,90,000, bought goods on credit for ₹54,000, sold goods costing ₹40,000 for ₹60,000 in cash and withdrew ₹8,000 for personal use. Without listing every step, find the capital at the end and explain why total assets rose by more than capital.
items.answer: Capital ₹5,02,000; assets ₹5,56,000, liabilities ₹54,000
items.markingKey: Capital = ₹4,90,000 + profit ₹20,000 − drawings ₹8,000 = ₹5,02,000 (2). Assets = ₹5,02,000 + creditors ₹54,000 = ₹5,56,000; the credit purchase raised assets and liabilities equally without changing capital (1).
